_comment: Example H6 validator schema. A reviewer's required structural elements are expressed as named regex patterns; H6 injects a re-invoke directive when the reviewer's output is missing any of them. This file ships as a documented example and as a test target — no `example-reviewer` agent is shipped. Copy it to <stem>.json for your own reviewer and replace the patterns with that reviewer's real required structure. See docs/provenance.md for why harness-layer validation exists.

required_patterns.name: verification-questions table (header row containing 'Question' between pipes)
risk or kill-case table (header row containing 'Risk', 'Condition', or 'Kill' between pipes)
verdict keyword (an ALL-CAPS SHIP / REVISE / REJECT on a word boundary)

feedback_template:
The reviewer output is missing structural elements its protocol requires. Re-invoke the reviewer with this framing prepended to your prompt:

  "BEFORE you address anything else — and overriding any structure I provide below — produce the required structural elements in order: one row per verification question; one row per risk / kill-case; then a single ALL-CAPS verdict. Then continue with the rest of your response."

This caller-side preamble is what makes the protocol stick: the agent prompt alone has been measured insufficient (see docs/provenance.md).
